newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Petsec sees 1997 sales up 30-40 pct on 1996.
newsitem.headline: Petsec sees 1997 sales up 30-40 pct on 1996.

text.p: Petsec Energy Ltd said on Monday it expected to boost sales of oil and gas in calendar 1997 by 30 to 40 percent on its 1996 sales of US$67.2 million.

"If production continues the way we anticipate then we see sales are going to be somewhere in the order of 30-40 percent higher than in the previous year," managing director Terry Fern told shareholders at the annual general meeting.
The 1996 sales figure of US$67.2 million was net of royalities.
Fern later told reporters Petsec expected to double net production in calendar 1997 to about 50 billion cubic feet equivalent (bcfe), and sales should be "in the order of US$100 million".
He expected production to rise a further 50 percent in calendar 1998 and 25-30 percent the following year.
"If we do 50 bcfe this year, we hope to something in the order of 75 bcfe the next year and 100 bcfe the year after that," Fern said.
Petsec, which operates in the Gulf of Mexico, earlier reported March quarter production of 919,282 barrels of oil and 7.275 bcf of gas, a rise of 50 percent on the December quarter.
Fern said much of the forecast production for the next two years would come from deposits which had already been discovered.
Petsec said it had 246 million bcfe of proved and probable reserves and a total of 892 million bcfe of potential reserves in both its production and exploration leases.

"With our reserves positions, if we get anywhere near the mapped potential then we are going to have enough reserves there for a reasonable life for perhaps three, four, five years after that," Fern said.

He also said growing competition in the Gulf of Mexico meant Petsec would consider exploration leases in shallow state waters and onshore, rather than simply in Federal leases, where the company has traditionally operated.
Fern said state waters were more complicated and more expensive, and would not be the company's main focus.
"All we are saying is if we don't get the inventory we want in our area then we will look at things and we will look at things in the shallower water," he said.
Petsec share were steady at A$4.90 at 2.05 p.m. (0405 GMT).
